findings.title: After-end note labels findings that were already sent back as "(not sent back)", which contradicts its own preface
findings.scenario: This is the exact v3.1 case: the check on the last turn sends back a missing file, then the cap cuts the run off. Repro via the Pi helper: ask(); bash('ls data'); ev('stop', turn=14, budget=15) returns continue, and the model receives "- The request asks for /app/answer.txt, but it does not exist...". Then ev('session_end', turn=15, budget=15, aborted=True). delivery.md says "Ended before the agent said it was done, after the stated 15 model turns; the last delivery check had sent it back." and, in the same note, "Not verified: Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist". The screen line says "Found after the run ended: 1 point(s)." The same false line appears when the capped turn is a final answer (session_end with final_answer=True). The finding has the same finding_id as round 1, so the record shows it was found before the end and was sent back. The fix hint below also covers a related issue: in the cut-off variant where the agent then writes the file (turn 15 has a tool call, run aborted), the note puts it under "## Redone before delivery", but nothing was delivered.
findings.fix: In _write_note with after_end: for findings whose finding_id appears in sess['rounds'] (or sess['open']), write "Sent back in round N, still there when the run ended" instead of "Found after the run ended (not sent back)". Keep "not sent back" only for ids that were never pushed. Retitle the fixed section when after_end is set (e.g. "Redone after being sent back").

findings.title: _reminded_writes counts a deletion (or chmod-only change) as "written" after the reminder
findings.scenario: step.writes is a workspace diff and includes kind "deleted" and exec-bit changes. Repro 1: ask(); bash writes scratch.py; turn(13) sends a nudge; bash('rm scratch.py'); session_end(turn=16, budget=15, aborted=True). The note says "- scratch.py: written at step 2, after the budget reminder sent after turn 13. The reminder asked for the current best answer...", the screen says "Written after a budget reminder: scratch.py.", and delivery.json has written_after_reminder=[{scratch.py, step 2}]. Step 2 was the rm, and the same note says "Files written in this turn: none". Repro 2: after the nudge, echo 2045 > answer.txt (step 2), then rm answer.txt (step 3). The note says "answer.txt: written at step 3, after the budget reminder" and also "answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist". Step 3 deleted the file; it did not write it. If exactly one deliverable exists and has no checked values, the deleted path also gets "Vacant checked no value in it against the record."
findings.fix: Skip changes with kind == 'deleted' (after is None) and changes where only the exec bit differs, e.g. `if isinstance(w, dict) and w.get('after') is None: last.pop(p, None); continue`. A path whose last change is a deletion then drops out, or is reported as "deleted at step k".

findings.title: "Nothing was written after it" is printed when the record says the writes are unknown; the cut-off note also newly says an existing file "did not exist"
findings.file_line: vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:441-451, 369 ; :577 replacing the os.path.exists-based line at :532-534
findings.scenario: When the scan is disabled (over 50k files, or an incremental scan took longer than 8 s), steps are recorded with writes=[] and writes_unknown set. CLAUDE.md: 'not known what was written' ≠ 'nothing written'. Repro: ask(); bash('cat data/sales.csv'); turn(13) sends a nudge; the scan then raises ValueError (file limit); bash writes answer.txt; session_end(turn=16, budget=15, aborted=True). delivery.md says "A budget reminder was sent after turn 13 (a requested file did not exist yet). Nothing was written after it." and "Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist". answer.txt exists on disk; the step after the nudge has writes_unknown='workspace has more than 50000 files'; the 'ended' event's own missing list is [] (computed with os.path.exists). Before v3.3 the cut-off note used budget.missing_outputs and correctly said "answer.txt: exists; its content was not checked." _reminded_writes also ignores unrecorded_change events (e.g. a background process writing the answer after the nudge).
findings.fix: In _reminded_writes, if any step of this session after the first nudge has writes_unknown, or an unrecorded_change event follows the nudge, write "what was written after it is not known (the workspace was not observed)" instead of "Nothing was written after it". In the after-end path, drop missing_output findings for paths that budget.exists() finds, or keep the v3.1 line for those paths.

findings.title: The after-end check runs under the 30 s session_end timeout, not the Stop limit, and a kill also skips the session close
findings.scenario: v3.3 runs the full delivery check (a subprocess with a 330 s limit) for cut-off runs too. The decision says 'the same child process and time limit'. But the extension passes TIMEOUT.stop only when `late` (a final answer); a cut-off run (aborted, last turn had tools) gets TIMEOUT.session_end = 30000 ms. In a project where the check takes 30–330 s, which the Stop path tolerates (for example a long-lived project chain that verify_since(None) must verify from genesis because no Stop check ran), the extension SIGKILLs `vacant hook pi session_end` at 30 s. No delivery note is written; v3.1 wrote its short note in under a second. The file left in place is the previous delivery.md, e.g. the "(sent back for another pass)" note from the last pushback, so the person reads a stale note. Because _zero_ended runs before _trace(session_end), the kill also loses Recorder.close: no session_closed, no transcript seal, and no final unrecorded_change.
findings.fix: Pass TIMEOUT.stop whenever ABORTED or late is true, or have the hook run _trace(session_end) first and do the after-end check in a detached process, as finalize does.

findings.title: The final-answer preface says "on the last of the stated N model turns; the run stopped there" when the turn is past N and the Stop check had run and failed
findings.scenario: v3.1 treats a budget that has been exceeded as unenforced, and v3.2 says that when the check did not run without an abort it was an error or a deferral, so nothing is added. But `late` and _said_done_unchecked use TURNS >= BUDGET, and at_cap uses turn_i >= budget_i. Repro: ask(); bash writes answer.txt; ev('stop', turn=20, budget=15) while the check child raises, which returns allow + DID_NOT_RUN and writes no review; session_end(turn=20, budget=15, aborted=False, final_answer=True) with the check working again. delivery.md says "The agent said it was done on the last of the stated 15 model turns; the run stopped there, before the delivery check could send anything back." In fact it was turn 20, nothing stopped the run, and the Stop check was attempted and failed. In interactive pi, TURNS is counted per process across requests, so turn > budget is reachable with a budget read from AGENTS.md.
findings.fix: Require turn == budget, not >=, for the 'said done unchecked' route and for the 'last of the stated N' wording. Otherwise use the neutral sentence, or skip when turn > budget and not aborted, as v3.1 does.

findings.title: A failed after-end check writes two 'ended' events for one run, which doubles ended_notes
findings.scenario: If the after-end runner raises (a crash, or TimeoutExpired from the 330 s child), _check_after_end appends ended{checked:false,error} and returns None; ended() then writes the short note and appends another ended{checked:false}. Repro: monkeypatch _run_child to raise; ask(); bash('ls data'); session_end(turn=16, budget=15, aborted=True). Result: 2 'ended' events [(False, 'RuntimeError: check crashed'), (False, None)]. ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py counts every 'ended' event as ended_notes, and analyze_local.py sums them, so this run is reported as 2 cut-off notes. This affects any evaluation run on a v3.3 or later wheel.
findings.fix: Don't append in _check_after_end's except branch. Return the error to ended() and put it in the single 'ended' event that ended() writes.

findings.title: Note after the end says a finding was "not sent back" when an earlier check already sent it back in the same request
findings.scenario: This is the Harbor flow that the v3.1 test covers. Turn 14 of 15: the agent says it is done. The stop check (turns_left=1) sends back 'The request asks for /app/answer.txt, but it does not exist'. The review event records sent=['z_437c168f94']. Turn 15 then ends by being capped, either as a cut-off (aborted=True) or as another final answer (final_answer=True). ended() passes its guard because reviews[-1].action=='continue', and _check_after_end passes every current finding as left_open. The note then says 'Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist'. The record shows that exact finding was sent back one turn earlier. In the final-answer variant, the header also says '...before the delivery check could send anything back', so the reader is told nothing was ever sent back. In the cut-off variant, the header says 'the last delivery check had sent it back' and the next section contradicts it. The same thing happens when a round-1 pushback at any turn is followed by a capped final answer: both sent-back findings are listed as 'not sent back'. Reproduced in /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/test_r6.py and test_r1.py (both pass, and the printed notes show the false line). This breaks the rule that notes must be literally true about the record.
findings.fix: In _check_after_end, split the findings using the session's rounds (sess['rounds'] / sess['open']). For findings that were sent back, write something like 'Sent back in round N; still there when the run ended'. Keep 'Found after the run ended (not sent back)' only for findings that no review ever sent. Make the final-answer 'said' sentence stop implying that nothing was sent back when this request has earlier reviews. Add an assertion for this line to test_a_run_sent_back_on_its_last_turn_and_then_cut_off_gets_a_note.

findings.title: Cut-off check after the end runs under the extension's 30 s session_end kill; a slow check leaves no note and no session_closed
findings.file_line: vacant_network/adapters/agents.py:422-427 (late only when LAST_FINAL; otherwise TIMEOUT.session_end=30000); vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:518 via _run_child (330 s, start_new_session=True)
findings.scenario: v3.3 now runs the full delivery check at session_end for an aborted run with no final answer. The extension passes the longer stop timeout only when `late`, which needs LAST_FINAL, so an aborted run with no final answer gets 30 s and is then SIGKILLed. End-to-end repro: the real extension in node, driving the real `python -m vacant_network hook pi session_end`, with the check child slowed to 40 s as a stand-in for a very large record (/tmp/claude-0/review_v33/slow/). session_shutdown returned after 30 s. There was no delivery.md, no 'ended' event, and also no 'session_closed' event, because _zero_ended runs before _trace(session_end). The orphaned `zerostop check` child (new session, so the kill does not reach it, and it has no timeout because its parent is dead) kept running and wrote zero_state.json later. v3.1 wrote the short note in under a second. The design (§八) says the check uses the same child and time limit (330 s) and that a check that cannot run falls back to the v3.1 short note; neither happens here. For scale, a 5000-step record took 3.1 s for this hook call, so roughly 50k steps, or a slow or loaded disk, is enough to hit the cut-off.
findings.fix: Send TIMEOUT.stop whenever ABORTED or late (not only late). Alternatively, write the v3.1 short note (and the 'ended' event) before starting the after-end check and overwrite them on success. Also run _trace(session_end) before the slow part, so a kill cannot drop session_closed.

findings.title: `turn >= budget` re-runs the check at quit and writes a false 'last of the stated N turns; the run stopped there' note for an over-budget run
findings.scenario: v3.1's rule is that a turn count above the stated budget means nobody enforces that budget (_turns_left returns None). The new fallback ignores that rule and uses >=. pi's TURNS also never resets across requests in one process. Example: a stated 'budget of 15 model turns', and the agent gives a final answer at turn 22, so settle ran and the stop check ran. The stop check timed out or errored, so no review event was written. At quit, the extension sends late=true, which also gives a 600 s timeout, and the hook routes to ended(final_answer=True). The check runs a second time (the heavy check that just timed out, run again while pi blocks at quit). The note says 'The agent said it was done on the last of the stated 15 model turns; the run stopped there, before the delivery check could send anything back.' Both parts are false: it was turn 22, and the check had run. Reproduced in /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/test_r3.py::test_over_budget_stop_check_timed_out_then_quit (check runs: 2, note shown). This also contradicts §七: a final answer with no abort and not at the cap is not re-checked.
findings.fix: Use turn == budget (and TURNS === BUDGET in the extension) for the no-abort fallback, so an over-budget count is treated as no budget, as v3.1 does.

findings.title: Check after the end runs before open steps are settled, so it reports an existing requested file as 'did not exist' (v3.1 said 'exists')
findings.file_line: vacant_network/adapters/hook.py:412-420 (_zero_ended called before _trace(session_end)); vacant_network/trace/evidence.py:465-472 (missing_output uses the recorded index only)
findings.scenario: The stop path calls _trace first so that steps with no post are settled before the check (integration#5). The session_end path runs the new full check first and settles afterwards. Example: a step whose post_tool was never recorded (the post hook was killed at its 30 s timeout or crashed) wrote /app/answer.txt, and then the run ends aborted. The after-end check reads only the recorded index. The note says 'Files written in this turn: none' and 'Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist'. The file is on disk, and the same hook call then records step 2 with writes=[answer.txt]. The v3.1 fallback for the same state checks disk and correctly says '/app/answer.txt: exists; its content was not checked.' Reproduced in /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/test_r5.py and test_r7.py.
findings.fix: Settle and close the session's open steps (call _trace for session_end, or Recorder.settle) before _zero_ended runs the check. Alternatively, have missing_output in the after-end path also check os.path.exists, as budget.exists does.

findings.title: Check-after-end failure appends two 'ended' events for one session end (ended_notes counted twice)
findings.scenario: When _run_child raises (for example TimeoutExpired after 330 s, or a crash), _check_after_end appends an 'ended' event (checked=False, error=...) and returns None. ended() then writes the fallback note and appends a second 'ended' event for the same session and window. ops/eval/harbor_vacant.py counts every 'ended' event as ended_notes += 1, and analyze_local.py / split_ended.py sum it, so any v3.3 batch run whose after-end check failed reports 2 notes for 1. Reproduced in /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/test_r3.py::test_check_after_end_failure_writes_two_ended_events (the two events have seq 5 and 6).
findings.fix: Do not append in the exception branch of _check_after_end. Return the error to ended() and include it in the single fallback 'ended' event.

result.severity: medium: the note for the person states something false; nothing sent to the model changes
result.evidence:
I reproduced this with the real hook.handle("pi", …) path, using the Pi helper and proj fixture from tests/test_zero_budget.py. The check ran in-process (zerostop._run_child = zerostop.check). The repro file is /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/f_notsentback/test_repro.py and all 3 cases ran.

Case 1, the v3.1 case (cut off after the check sends the run back):
- Steps: ask(); bash("ls data"); ev("stop", final_text="Done.", turn=14, budget=15) returns action=continue. The model receives "- The request asks for /app/answer.txt, but it does not exist. ... Model turns left in the stated budget: 1 of 15." Then ev("session_end", reason="quit", turn=15, budget=15, aborted=True).
- The record has review event action=continue with sent=["z_44fbee51bc"]. zero_state.json has rounds=[{round:1, findings:[z_44fbee51bc missing_output answer.txt]}] and open=["z_44fbee51bc"]. The ended event lists the same finding_id z_44fbee51bc.
- delivery.md contains both of these lines:
  - "- Ended before the agent said it was done, after the stated 15 model turns; the last delivery check had sent it back. The check ran afterwards, ..."
  - under "## Not verified": "- Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist"
- The second line is false about the record. That finding was found before the end and was sent back in round 1, and the note's own opening line says so.

Case 2, final answer on the capped turn after a send-back:
- Same steps, then session_end(turn=15, budget=15, aborted=True, final_answer=True).
- The note contains the same false line: "Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt ... did not exist".

Case 3, the agent writes the file after the send-back and is then cut off:
- The note puts it under "## Redone before delivery: round 1: answer.txt ... it was written afterwards", although the run was aborted. This part is debatable: the workspace is what gets graded.

Cause:
- `_check_after_end` (zerostop.py:577) passes every current finding as left_open with after_end set.
- `_write_note` (lines 382-384 and 421-423) labels every left_open item "Found after the run ended (not sent back)", and the screen line "Found after the run ended: N point(s)", without checking sess["rounds"] or sess["open"]. Those hold the ids that were already pushed back.

When it came in:
- The cut-off branch is new in v3.3; the final_answer branch came in v3.2. Before these changes, this case wrote the short v3.1 note ("answer.txt: does not exist"), which was accurate.
- The existing test test_a_run_sent_back_on_its_last_turn_and_then_cut_off_gets_a_note only checks the opening line, so it does not catch the contradiction.
- Decision §八 says the cut-off note's opening should say whether the last check sent the run back, and CLAUDE.md requires claims in notes to be literally true about the record. The body line breaks both.

Model-facing text is not affected: the continue reason is identical and session_end returns {"action":"allow","reason":""}.

I reproduced this through the real hook.handle("pi", ...) using the Pi driver and proj fixture from tests/test_zero_budget.py. The test files are in /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/del/: test_repro_del.py and test_repro_del3.py. No repo file was modified.

Cause: in workspace.diff(), a step's `writes` holds every Change, including kind "deleted" (after=None) and exec-bit-only changes. _reminded_writes (zerostop.py:432-457) records every entry of `step.writes` in `last[p]` and never looks at kind or `after`.

Repro 1 (cut-off run). Steps: ask, then bash writes scratch.py (step 1, added), then turn(13) sends a nudge, then bash `rm scratch.py` (step 2, recorded as `('scratch.py','deleted')`), then session_end with turn=16, budget=15, aborted=True. The note in delivery.md says:
- "Files written in this turn: none"
- "scratch.py: written at step 2, after the budget reminder sent after turn 13. The reminder asked for the current best answer; ..."
delivery.json has written_after_reminder=[{'path':'scratch.py','step':2,'after_turn':13}].

Repro 2. Steps: turn(13), then echo 2045 > answer.txt (step 2, added), then rm answer.txt (step 3, deleted), then session_end aborted. The note says "answer.txt: written at step 3, after the budget reminder sent after turn 13" and, in the same note, "Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist". Step 3 was the deletion, so the two lines contradict each other.

Repro 3 (normal stop path, one deliverable). Steps: turn(13), then write answer.txt ('Not Applicable'), then rm scratch.py, then stop, which returns allow. The screen note returned in `note` (shown to the person via ctx.ui.notify) says "Written after a budget reminder: answer.txt, scratch.py." The md note says "scratch.py: written at step 4, ... Vacant checked no value in it against the record." But scratch.py was deleted at step 4, and "Files written in this turn" lists only answer.txt.

The existing test test_a_file_written_before_the_reminder_is_not_marked only covers a deletion before the reminder, which is why this passes the current tests.

Scope: the claims are false in text meant for the person: delivery.md, delivery.json and the screen notify. That breaks the rule that "claims in notes must be literally true about the record". Nothing is sent to the model, and no agent is blocked.

Suggested fix: in _reminded_writes, when `after` is None, do `last.pop(p, None)` (or report it as deleted), and skip changes where only the exec bit differs.

I reproduced this through the real `hook.handle("pi", …)`. The repro is /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/test_repro_unknown_writes.py, and all 4 cases pass on HEAD.

Scenario:
1. ask(ASK); the request says "Write the answer to /app/answer.txt".
2. bash("cat data/sales.csv").
3. turn_check(13, budget=15) sends a nudge.
4. Before the next step, the workspace passes the file limit. `test_real_50k_files_after_nudge` really creates 50,005 files (no monkeypatch). A variant sets `W.MAX_FILES` lower and runs both in-process and with the real `_run_child` subprocess.
5. The next bash step writes answer.txt.
6. session_end(turn=16, budget=15, aborted=True).

What the record then holds:
- A coverage event with scan_disabled="workspace has more than 50000 files…".
- Step 2 has writes=[] and writes_unknown set to that same text.
- The 'ended' event has missing=[] (from budget.exists, i.e. os.path.exists) and checked=True, with findings=[missing_output answer.txt].
- answer.txt exists on disk.

delivery.md on HEAD says:
"- A budget reminder was sent after turn 13 (a requested file did not exist yet). Nothing was written after it."
"- Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist"

Both lines are false. The record says the writes are unknown, not that there were none (the rule in CLAUDE.md is that "not known what was written" is not "nothing written"). The file also exists.

Regression check: I extracted the pre-change code with `git archive 5f3339df vacant_network` into /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/old and ran the same scenario. The old cut-off note says "/app/answer.txt: exists; its content was not checked. A budget reminder was sent after turn 13." So v3.3 routes cut-off runs through `_check_after_end`, which uses Evidence.run's missing_output. That check only looks at the recorded latest index (evidence.py:466-473), not `budget.exists`. The v3.2 final-answer path has the same issue.

Second case: `test_unrecorded_change_after_nudge`. answer.txt is written between steps after the nudge, and the next step's scan records an `unrecorded_change` adding answer.txt. The note still says "Nothing was written after it." The cause is that `_reminded_writes` (zerostop.py:441-451) counts only `step.writes`; it ignores `writes_unknown` and `unrecorded_change` events.

Scope:
- Only the note to the person (delivery.md/json and the screen message) is affected. `ended()` sends nothing to the model.
- A missing_output finding when the scan is disabled could already be sent back on the normal Stop path before this change, so model-facing behaviour is not newly changed by this diff.
- It needs the scan disabled (over 50k files, or an incremental scan over 8 s) or a write that no step explains after the reminder.

findings.title: After-end note says a finding was 'not sent back' and that the check had not sent anything back, when the check did send it back one turn earlier
findings.file_line: vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py:383 (also :507-510, the final_answer 'said' sentence in ended())
findings.scenario: Stated budget of 15 turns (Harbor). On turn 14 the agent gives a final answer without writing /app/answer.txt. The stop check runs with turns_left=1 and returns 'continue' with 'The request asks for /app/answer.txt, but it does not exist...'; the record gets a review event with action=continue and sent=[missing_output]. On turn 15 the agent replies in text only, and the cap aborts. The extension sends late=true with final_answer=true. hook._said_done_unchecked then routes to ended(final_answer=True), and because reviews[-1].action=='continue', ended() skips its early return and calls _check_after_end. Reproduced through hook.handle('pi', ...) with stop(turn=14, budget=15) -> continue, then session_end(turn=15, budget=15, aborted=True, final_answer=True). delivery.md then says: 'The agent said it was done on the last of the stated 15 model turns; the run stopped there, before the delivery check could send anything back.' and 'Found after the run ended (not sent back): answer.txt (asked for in the request) did not exist'. Both statements are false about the record. The same false line appears in the cut-off variant, the scenario of the existing test test_a_run_sent_back_on_its_last_turn_and_then_cut_off_gets_a_note. There the header says '...the last delivery check had sent it back' and the next line says the same finding was '(not sent back)', so the note contradicts itself. This breaks the rule that notes must be literally true about the record. The model receives nothing different.
findings.fix: In _check_after_end, pass sess['open'] (or the round ids) into _write_note. Write findings that were already sent back as 'Sent back in round N; still open when the run ended', and keep '(not sent back)' only for findings that were never pushed. In ended(), build the final_answer sentence from `reviews`: when the last review was 'continue', say the check had sent it back and the agent's last answer came after that.

findings.title: Check after a cut-off run gets only the pi extension's 30 s session_end limit; a slower check is SIGKILLed and no note is written at all (the v3.1 short note is lost)
findings.scenario: v3.3 made ended() run the full delivery check through _check_after_end for every aborted run, including final_answer=False (cap cut-off, Esc, or SIGTERM during a run). The pi extension extends the ask() timeout to TIMEOUT.stop only when LAST_FINAL is true. For a cut-off run it still uses session_end: 30000 and SIGKILLs the hook when that expires. The decision (section 8) promises 'the same child and time limit' (330 s) and a fallback to the v3.1 short note when the check cannot run. Neither holds when the check takes more than about 30 s. Repro, using the real extension in node and the real `vacant hook pi`, with evidence_for slowed to 40 s through a sitecustomize shim: tool steps, then Esc (ctl.abort() plus a tool result), then session_shutdown({reason:'quit'}). session_shutdown returned after 30005 ms, and the project's trace dir had no delivery.md and no 'ended' event. The pre-change build writes the short note in about 150 ms in the same scenario. The orphaned check child (start_new_session=True) also keeps running after the hook dies. The model receives nothing different; the loss is the note for the person.
findings.fix: Use the same `late`-style extended timeout (TIMEOUT.stop) whenever ABORTED is true. Alternatively, in ended(), write and append the v3.1 short note and the 'ended' event before starting the check, then overwrite them with the full note when the check returns.

findings.title: `turn >= budget` in _said_done_unchecked and in the extension's `late` ignores v3.1's 'over the stated budget means no budget' rule: quit re-runs the check and the note makes false claims
findings.scenario: Interactive pi where the system prompt carries an unenforced budget sentence, e.g. AGENTS.md says 'at most 10 turns'. TURNS never resets within the process, so after 25 turns every request ends with LAST_FINAL=true and TURNS>=BUDGET. If the in-turn stop check failed (exception or 330 s timeout, so DID_NOT_RUN and no review event), quitting pi sets late=true. The extension then waits up to 600 s while pi's TUI has already stopped, and the hook re-runs the whole check (up to 330 s). Reproduced via hook.handle: stop(turn=25, budget=10) with a failing runner returns allow and 'Vacant check did not run'; then session_end(turn=25, budget=10, final_answer=True, aborted=False). delivery.md says: 'The agent said it was done on the last of the stated 10 model turns; the run stopped there, before the delivery check could send anything back.' Since v3.3, zerostop.ended() always calls `_check_after_end` → `_run_child`, which allows 330 s (CHECK_TIMEOUT_S). The fallback to the short note only happens when that call returns or raises, which never occurs if the parent is SIGKILLed first. In hook.handle, `_zero_ended` runs before `_trace(session_end)`, so killing the hook also drops `session_closed`. That loses Recorder.end_session's closing of open steps, the stop-marking of sub-agents, and the unrecorded_change scan at session end.

Interactive pi does take this path on any Esc-aborted last request followed by quit, with or without a budget. Nothing sent to the model is affected; only the person's note and the record's session_closed are lost. Minor is the right severity.

Fix options: pass TIMEOUT.stop whenever ABORTED || late; or write the v3.1 note and the 'ended' event first and overwrite them on success; or run `_trace(session_end)` before the slow part.

Step 1, real node extension. A fake interactive pi has a system prompt containing "use at most 10 turns" (it matches BUDGET_RE). It runs two requests of 12 and 13 turns, each ending in a final answer and a stop check that returns allow, then quits. TURNS is never reset per request, so the stop payloads carry turn/budget (12,10) and (25,10). The session_end payload is {turn:25, budget:10, aborted:false, final_answer:true, final_text:"Done: second"}. final_text is only sent when `late` is true, so `late` was true: the quit uses TIMEOUT.stop (600 s) instead of 30 s. `hook._said_done_unchecked(payload)` is True.

Step 2, real hook.handle:
1. ask, then ls data, then write answer.txt.
2. Stop with turn=25, budget=10 while _run_child raises. Result: {'action':'allow', 'note':'Vacant check did not run (error recorded).'}, and no review event.
3. session_end with reason=quit, turn=25, budget=10, aborted=False, final_answer=True.

The check re-ran once at the end. The `ended` event records turn 25 and budget 10. delivery.md contains: "- The agent said it was done on the last of the stated 10 model turns; the run stopped there, before the delivery check could send anything back. The check ran afterwards, for you only". That is false on two counts. It was turn 25 of an unenforced 10-turn budget, and the note's own record says turn 25. Also, the run did not stop because of the cap; the in-turn check was tried and failed.

Control: the identical situation at turn=5, budget=10, and with no budget at all, writes no `ended` note and runs no re-check. The existing test test_a_final_answer_before_the_cap_without_an_abort_gets_no_note describes that as intended ("the check didn't run = error or defer, don't redo it"). So a run over the budget is handled like a run at the cap, which contradicts v3.1's "over the budget means no budget".

Scope of the defect:
- It only triggers when the in-turn stop check leaves no review event: an exception, the 330 s timeout, a broken chain, or the extension killing the hook. A normal allow writes a review and ended() returns early.
- Nothing reaches the model: session_end returns {'action':'allow','reason':''}. The damage is a false sentence in the person-only note, plus up to 330 s of re-check (the extension waits up to 600 s) on quit.

The same repro against 1685e664 (v3.4, committed during this review) passes: `_said_done_unchecked` returns False, no delivery.md is written, and the extension omits final_text. That commit applies exactly the suggested fix: `turn == budget` in hook.py, `TURNS === BUDGET` in agents.py, and `at_cap = turn_i == budget_i`.

I reproduced this against the reviewed code: a2b4b0ee, whose vacant_network is byte-identical to 9ac91c18, the HEAD when the task was issued. I used `git archive` to extract that tree into /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/v33 and made no changes to the repo.

Setup (all under /tmp/claude-0/review_v33/repro_to):
- The real extension is built from `AG.PI_EXTENSION` with the installed values: argv = [venv python, -m, vacant_network, hook, pi] and timeout_ms = 600000. It runs in node 22 and calls the real `vacant hook pi`.
- A fresh HOME and VACANT_HOME, with install.json set to mode evidence.
- A sitecustomize shim (`site/sitecustomize.py`) adds 40 s to `trace.evidence.evidence_for`, which only the check child calls.
- The driver (`drive.tmpl.mjs`) sends before_agent_start, then tool_call/tool_result/turn_end with toolResults, then a second tool_call, then `ctl.abort()` (the Esc), a tool_result and turn_end (stopReason `aborted`), and finally `session_shutdown({reason:'quit'})`.
- `run.sh` runs it and `peek.py` inspects the record.

Code path: in the v3.3 extension, `late` needs LAST_FINAL, so a cut-off run gets `ms = undefined`, which falls back to `TIMEOUT.session_end = 30000` (agents.py:427, `late ? TIMEOUT.stop : undefined`). The hook sees aborted=True, then `_zero_ended`, then `ended(final_answer=False)`, then `_check_after_end`, then `_run_child`, whose own limit is 330 s. In HEAD, `handle()` also runs `_zero_ended` before `_trace`, so a SIGKILL loses the session_end step too.

Results:
- **v3.3 with a 40 s check:** session_shutdown returned after 30005 ms. The trace dir had no delivery.md. The events were [trace_genesis, prompt, session_seen, step, step]: no 'ended' and no 'session_closed'. The shim log shows the orphaned check child (start_new_session=True) kept running and finished 40 s after it started, about 10 s after the hook was killed.
- **v3.3 with no slowdown (control):** returned after 310 ms. It wrote the full after-the-end note and an ended event with checked=true, so the only difference is the time limit.
- **Before the change (5f3339df), same 40 s shim:** returned after 170 ms and wrote the v3.1 short note ("Ended before the agent said it was done; no delivery check ran.") plus 'ended' and 'session_closed'. So v3.3 turns a note that used to be written into no note at all whenever the check takes more than about 30 s.

This contradicts two things in DECISION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3.md §八: the check is supposed to get the same child process and time limit, and a check that cannot run is supposed to fall back to the v3.1 short note.

Nothing sent to the model changes. The only loss is the note for the person. Measured stop checks in `ops/eval/evidence_*` take 0.4–1 s, so this needs an unusually slow check (large record or workspace, or a loaded machine). That is why I rate it minor.

TIMEOUT.stop : undefined` and moves `_trace` before `_zero_ended`. The same repro against that tree (/tmp/claude-0/review_v33/v34) returned after 40323 ms and wrote delivery.md, 'session_closed' and 'ended' (checked=true).
